scope: Desktop WeChat DevTools simulator; no phone or preview action
entry: Existing Map example spot -> cloud sky -> manual drag mode -> two-touch zoom

context.orientation: manual, not a measured phone pose

pixelObservation.method: Raw PNG sampled in several 54x45-pixel rectangular windows at stride 3, excluding bright star pixels with R>=45 or G>=45 or B>=60; rounded mean RGB per window
pixelObservation.interpretation: A broad diagonal diffuse band is visible in the ordinary night sky image. Current code submits the coordinate-based galactic shader at this exact frame and FOV; the observation does not establish photometric or contour accuracy.
pixelObservation.modeTransition: At unchanged 248.4 degree FOV and report time, Settings selected Observation red -> Sky showed a black background with warm-red stars/grid and no cool diffuse band. Restoring Day mode returned the ordinary broad diffuse band. The page-level program also skips galacticBand in Observation mode.
pixelObservation.maximumDomeCorrection: 248.4 degrees was an intermediate zoom: its horizon circle is clipped at the left/right viewport edge. A second outward pinch reached the actual 267.8-degree maximum, where the complete horizon circle has visible margins on both sides. No projection code repair is warranted from the intermediate screenshot.

runtime.officialSkyAria: 4069 catalog objects, 2026-09-22T13:00:00.000Z, manual basis, 128.8 then 248.4 then maximum 267.8 degree FOV
runtime.consoleFilter: grep -n -i 'sky_gpu|error|shader' empty before wide capture and after mode restoration
